title: Prove sampled positioning stability in the z-plane
physicalPurpose: Prove stability for the sample, hold, computation delay, and controller realization that actually execute.
principalTechnique: Exact hold discretization and z-plane stability
objective: Explain and verify why unchanged continuous gains fail at 100 ms and validate a corrected digital position controller.

simplifications: Measured position and velocity without sensor noise in the motion run
Exact zero-order-hold analysis with explicit one-sample delay
Ideal force response inside declared limits
No friction, backlash, structural flex, end-stop contact, current loop, or thermal protection

baseline.limitation: The unchanged gains create a sampled pole pair of magnitude 1.04126 and therefore an unstable 100 ms implementation.

change.decision: Accept the corrected controller only when exact augmented poles and bounded executable motion agree under the actual sample, hold, delay, and limits.

disturbances: Analysis-only 40 rad/s alias calculation; no injected motion-run disturbance

acceptance.window: exact augmented 10 ms model with one-sample delay
exact augmented 100 ms model with unchanged gains and one-sample delay
exact augmented 100 ms model with corrected gains and one-sample delay
mean absolute error over 9 through 10 seconds after settling qualification
mean absolute error over 9 through 10 seconds after settling qualification

abortPredicates: Any required signal is missing, stale, forced, nonfinite, or has bad quality
Any requested force leaves minus 10 through plus 10 percent
Any carriage position leaves minus 5 through plus 5 millimetres
Actual sample, hold, delay, gain, plant, limit, timing, or evidence class differs from the reviewed case
safety.restorationMode: Latch the affected normal controller out, apply the reviewed velocity-damping controlled stop until motion ceases, disable the experiment, restore zero force and position request, and restart the simulated table at its reviewed initial state
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised motion-control engineer and responsible machine operator
simulationOnlyRestrictions: The lesson does not move a physical table
Simulation pole and stop evidence cannot authorise physical motion
Physical execution requires independent drive topology, force, current, speed, travel, end-stop, guard, emergency-stop, motion-zone, stopping-distance, abort, rollback, and immediate approval review

video.viewerOutcome: Prove a sampled position loop in the z-plane and recover an unstable coarse implementation with a qualified discrete redesign.
requiredVisibleEvidence: unit circle and discrete root locus
bounded unstable trace and controlled stop

learning.context: Three equivalent positioning tables isolate fine sampling, unchanged coarse sampling, and corrected coarse digital gains.
learning.reason: A continuous design does not include the sample, hold, computation delay, or realization that the PLC executes.
theory: The z-transform represents sampled sequences and one-sample delay.
The unit circle is the discrete stability boundary.
Exact zero-order hold maps plant dynamics and creates sampling zeros.
Nyquist frequency bounds unique sampled content and higher content aliases.
A discrete root locus traces z-plane poles as digital gain changes.
learning.workedPrediction: Calculate exact hold matrices, zeros, augmented poles, unit-circle magnitudes, Nyquist limits, and alias frequency before motion.
practicalPreparation: Verify equivalent mechanics, signals, units, sample and hold timing, delay, force and position limits, abort, controlled stop, seed, and Simulation status.
Record the stable, unstable, and corrected predictions before enabling the common move.
learning.baseline: Apply the continuous-design gains at 100 ms with one-sample delay and stop the predicted unstable motion safely.
learning.change: At the same 100 ms interval and delay, reduce only proportional gain to the qualified discrete value.
learning.comparison: Compare exact pole evidence with equivalent motion and force records without allowing early appearance to override z-plane stability.
learning.validation: Require analytical and Control Studio agreement plus bounded fine, failed coarse, and recovered corrected execution.
learning.explanation: Longer hold and explicit delay move the unchanged-gain pole pair outside the unit circle; corrected gain restores stability at a speed cost.
learning.transfer: Digital stability belongs to the executed sample, hold, delay, realization, limits, and timing; Lesson 51 can now compare tuning methods fairly.
